title: ABM Pilot (Regulated Workloads) — Project Plan + Weekly Standup Notes
content:
Doc purpose
- Single working doc to keep the 6–8 week ABM pilot moving: weekly goals, owners, decisions, open questions, and the “what changed” log.
- Pilot theme: regulated workloads (FinServ + Healthcare) with emphasis on Hosted → Dedicated → Private (VPC/on-prem) path, security-forward messaging, and faster security review.

Pilot north star + success definition (draft)
North star
- Prove we can generate qualified meetings + convert a subset into POC scoping + progress security review faster than baseline when Private/VPC is in the narrative.

Success (what we’ll call “works” at end of pilot)
- Meetings: 12–18 qualified meetings across the 2 verticals (CISO/GRC + Platform/ML mix), with ≥40% from Tier 1 accounts.
- POCs: 4–6 scoped evaluations with success criteria documented and an agreed security review plan.
- Security progression: ≥3 accounts moving past “initial security questions” into questionnaire exchange / evidence review.
- Pipeline: at least 2 opportunities with clear Dedicated or Private next step and named stakeholders in security + platform.

Guardrails / non-goals
- Do not over-promise: Private installer maturity, audit log retention specifics, “no data stored” absolutes, HIPAA/BAA statements, or region availability beyond what Security/GRC has approved.
- This is a packaging + repeatability test, not a brand campaign.

Scope / vertical focus
Verticals in scope
- Financial Services (banks, payments, wealth, regtech)
- Healthcare (payer/provider networks + healthtech platforms with PHI constraints)

Primary personas + narrative angle
- CISO / Security Eng / GRC: auditability, data boundaries, encryption/KMS/HSM options, retention + residency controls, evidence availability (SOC2 posture), operational responsibilities
- Platform Engineering: deployment models, VPC networking and controls, reliability + fallbacks, integrations (SIEM/log export), SSO/RBAC, operational model
- ML Engineering: latency/throughput predictability, cost per token, caching/batching, model selection + rollouts
- Data/Privacy: data handling boundaries, retention controls, residency, DPA/BAA questions routed to counsel

Core problem thesis (approved direction)
- Regulated teams need predictable inference performance + flexible deployment boundaries + audit-ready controls without building/operating the entire serving stack.

Workstreams + owners
1) Messaging + assets
- Owner: Soojin Lee (PMM)
- Contributors: Ethan Wallace (Content), Ben Carter (Growth), Markus Klein (SE review), Dr. Aisha Rahman / Olga Petrov (Security/GRC review)

2) Targeting + outbound
- Owner: Grace O’Connor (SDR program)
- Contributors: Rohan Mehta (SDR), AEs (Avery Johnson, Priyom Das, Hannah Schmitt, Diego Fernandez), Isabelle Laurent (analytics)

3) Security acceleration pack
- Owner: Kevin Osei (Security FAQs) / Olga Petrov (GRC)
- Contributors: Marcus Lin (Security Eng), Daniel Carter (questionnaire support), Soojin (language alignment)

4) Reference architecture + Private technical narrative
- Owner: Simran Kaur (Reference architect)
- Contributors: Colin O’Donnell (Private discovery), Markus Klein / Fatima Noor (SE), Elliot Price / Kira Thompson (Docs)

5) Conversion + routing + measurement
- Owner: Tyler Benson (Mops)
- Contributors: Ben Carter (Growth), Isabelle Laurent (reporting), Engineering (ENG-2941), Product (PM-482)

Key assets (minimum set)
- Landing pages: FinServ regulated workloads + Healthcare regulated workloads (plus shared “Regulated” overview)
- Pitch deck: FinServ (Private/VPC talk track) + Healthcare (PHI framing)
- Security FAQ addendum: FinServ + Healthcare (questionnaire-ready language)
- Private/VPC reference architecture diagram + responsibilities matrix
- Persona objection-handling matrix (internal)

Timeline (target)
- Week 0–1: kickoff, ICP + target lists, messaging, metrics and routing, outbound drafts
- Week 2–3: asset creation + internal enablement + security/GRC approval loop
- Week 3–6: outbound live + weekly iteration; discovery/demos; POC scoping
- Week 6–8: security questionnaires + evidence packaging; procurement prep; retro + scale decision

Metrics + reporting notes (draft)
Funnel metrics (weekly)
- Target account engagement: email reply rate, meetings booked, landing page CVR (form fill / visit), webinar registration + attendance
- Meetings → POC: # POC candidates, # scoped POCs with written success criteria
- Security: # questionnaire exchanges, # evidence requests, time-to-first-security-call
- Pipeline: # opps created, stage movement, deployment preference (Dedicated vs Private) captured as a field

Attribution basics
- All ABM landing page and webinar traffic must carry UTMs (source/medium/campaign/content) and map to HubSpot.
- Form routing rules: FinServ vs Healthcare, region, and “Private interest” checkbox → Slack notifications to #sales + SE channel.

Open questions (top-of-mind, keep updated)
1) “Do you store prompts/outputs?” — confirm final language per deployment mode and logging configuration. Owner: Olga / Aisha. Status: in progress.
2) “Audit logs” — what is GA vs limited, how exports work, default retention. Owner: Marcus Lin. Status: awaiting final wording in FAQ.
3) HIPAA/BAA handling — what we can say without Legal review; clarify routing to Sofia Mendes for anything contractual. Owner: Camila / Sofia. Status: pending.
4) On-prem positioning — when to propose on-prem vs VPC vs Dedicated; confirm current installer readiness in messaging. Owner: Vivek Kulkarni / Simran. Status: needs product check.
5) Region/residency commitments — what regions are actually supportable for regulated workloads today; approved roadmap-safe phrasing. Owner: Aisha / Olga. Status: in review.

Decision log
- 2026-01-08: Run two vertical variants (FinServ + Healthcare) rather than a single “regulated” generic page. Rationale: different objections + compliance language. Owner: Soojin.
- 2026-01-10: Default CTA for regulated pages = “Schedule a security/architecture review” (not “Start for free”) to match intent + reduce unqualified signups. Owner: Ben/Tyler.
- 2026-01-15: Keep “HIPAA-ready” out of top-level headlines; use “PHI-aware deployment patterns” and route BAA talk to sales/legal. Owner: Aisha/Olga.
- 2026-01-22: Add a short responsibilities matrix (Redwood vs Customer) into the Private reference architecture asset. Owner: Simran.
- 2026-02-04: Webinar format = 35 min talk + 10 min demo + 15 min security Q&A (moderated). Owner: Noura.

Risk log (update weekly)
- Risk: Over-promising security/compliance posture in public-facing assets.
  - Mitigation: security-reviewed FAQ addendum; “approved phrasing vs risky claims” checklist; final sign-off in #eng-security.
- Risk: Form routing + attribution breaks → can’t measure pilot.
  - Mitigation: ENG-2941 instrumentation + QA checklist + test submissions per vertical.
- Risk: SDR bandwidth + account coverage conflicts with existing quotas.
  - Mitigation: narrow Tier 1 list; explicit assignment + AE confirmation in #sales.
- Risk: Too many bespoke security answers → slow cycle time.
  - Mitigation: standard questionnaire-ready snippets + evidence package index.

Weekly standup notes

Week 0 (Kickoff) — 2026-01-06
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Grace, Tyler, Markus, Fatima, Aisha, Olga, Isabelle
This week’s goals
- Confirm verticals + initial ICP and persona map
- Lock pilot success metrics + required HubSpot fields (PM-482)
- Draft messaging framework + “approved vs risky” claim list
- Start target list compilation (FinServ + Healthcare)
Progress
- Soojin started regulated narrative doc + persona value props
- Grace + AEs started FinServ target list tiering discussion
- Aisha/Olga requested central place for retention/residency language
Decisions
- Treat Private/VPC story as primary differentiator; Dedicated as step for predictable throughput when Private not required
Action items
- Soojin: draft messaging v0 for review (due 1/09)
- Tyler: outline UTM + routing requirements for ENG-2941 (due 1/09)
- Grace: propose Tier 1 criteria + account assignment draft (due 1/10)
Open questions added
- “Do we sign BAAs?” route to Legal; need approved talking points.

Week 1 — 2026-01-13
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Ethan, Grace, Tyler, Markus, Aisha, Olga, Isabelle
This week’s goals
- Outbound sequence drafts + subject lines
- Start deck outlines; create asset checklist + owners
- Confirm what evidence can be shared pre-NDA
Progress
- Email sequence copy reviewed in #sales (feedback: too much “developer-first,” not enough “risk reduction”)
- Aisha/Olga: initial pass on what we can say publicly vs under NDA
- Markus: asked for a concise KMS/HSM options paragraph to reuse in replies
Decisions
- Sequence structure: 1) “regulatory pressure + deployment choice” 2) “Private/VPC reference architecture” 3) “security FAQ pack” 4) “offer: 30-min architecture review”
Action items
- Ethan: rewrite email 1–2 to lead with auditability + boundaries; send to Security for check (due 1/15)
- Markus/Fatima: draft KMS/HSM integration explainer snippet (due 1/16)
- Isabelle: finalize baseline dashboard spec (draft) for weekly review (due 1/17)
Notes / feedback
- AEs want clearer “what happens in a POC” one-paragraph summary to reduce back-and-forth.

Week 2 — 2026-01-20
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Tyler, Noura, Markus, Simran, Aisha, Olga
This week’s goals
- First drafts: landing page copy, deck content, security FAQ addenda
- Reference architecture: diagram + responsibilities matrix draft
- Confirm webinar concept + date range
Progress
- Soojin delivered FinServ deck outline + talk track (SE requested more “operational boundaries” slide)
- Simran shared reference architecture draft: VPC boundaries, logging pipeline, KMS/HSM integration points
- Security review flagged ambiguous statements about retention defaults
Decisions
- All assets must include “deployment boundary” callouts (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private): what flows where, what customer controls
Action items
- Olga: finalize “retention/residency positioning” snippet library (due 1/24)
- Tyler/Ben: ensure landing page form includes checkbox for “VPC/Private required” + “security review request” (due 1/24)
- Noura: draft webinar run-of-show + speaker list (due 1/24)
Asset feedback backlog
- Replace “compliant” with “supports compliance workflows / controls” (Security)
- Add “audit log export to SIEM” phrasing but avoid naming unsupported formats (Security/SE)

Week 3 — 2026-01-27
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Ethan, Grace, Tyler, Markus, Colin, Aisha, Olga, Isabelle
This week’s goals
- Finalize v1 assets for internal enablement
- Start outbound to Tier 1 accounts
- Get docs PRs moving (ENG-2960 / redwood-docs PR)
Progress
- Landing page copy in final edits; Legal/Security checklist started
- Grace: SDR plays ready; waiting on final target list assignment
- Docs: plan to publish “Private deployment reference architecture” page for discoverability
Issues
- Confusion on “audit logs: available today vs planned” causing edits loop
Decisions
- Keep security FAQ addendum as the canonical place for detailed security statements; landing pages link out and stay high-level
Action items
- Aisha/Marcus: finalize audit log language + what evidence can be shared under NDA (due 1/31)
- Grace: finalize account assignment + owner mapping in #sales (due 1/29)
- Markus/Colin: create a 10-question discovery checklist for Private/VPC fits (due 1/31)
Notes
- We should pre-brief AEs on “when to walk away” criteria (e.g., required certifications we don’t have).

Week 4 — 2026-02-03
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Noura, Tyler, Markus, Fatima, Aisha, Olga, Isabelle
This week’s goals
- Outbound live + first iteration loop (replies, objections)
- Partner intro call and co-marketing plan
- Webinar dry run scheduled
Progress
- Initial replies show strongest resonance: “VPC deployment + auditability + predictable latency”
- Common objection: “Do you keep prompts/outputs? For how long?” (needs crisp answer)
- Partner motion: align on lead sharing + logo approvals
Decisions
- Add a short “Data handling boundaries (Hosted vs Private)” section to both landing pages (one paragraph + link to FAQ)
Action items
- Soojin/Ethan: add data boundaries paragraph + send to Security for sign-off (due 2/05)
- Tyler: confirm lead sharing fields + UTMs for partner webinar landing page (due 2/06)
- Isabelle: start weekly “ABM snapshot” template (due 2/07)

Week 5 — 2026-02-10
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Ethan, Noura, Tyler, Markus, Simran, Aisha, Olga
This week’s goals
- Webinar dry run; finalize demo flow
- Tighten POC packaging + mutual action plan template for regulated accounts
- Reduce security review friction (FAQ + evidence index)
Progress
- Dry run feedback: demo timing ran long; security Q&A needs pre-written answers for top 8 questions
- SE request: include “VPC peering / DNS/TLS assumptions” appendix in reference architecture
Decisions
- Webinar Q&A will be moderated with pre-answered “most asked” questions (security-first), and any contractual items deferred
Action items
- Markus/Simran: produce appendix for network assumptions (peering, DNS, TLS) (due 2/13)
- Olga/Daniel: build “evidence package index” list (what’s available under NDA) (due 2/13)
- Jasmine Liu: draft CS/SE handoff notes template for regulated POCs (due 2/14)

Week 6 — 2026-02-18
Attendees: Camila, Soojin, Ben, Grace, Tyler, Markus, Aisha, Olga, Isabelle, Jordan
This week’s goals
- Midpoint exec update: what’s working, what’s stuck, what we’re changing
- Double down on the best-performing messaging + channels
- Identify 4–6 POC candidates and align resources
Snapshot (qualitative)
- Strongest segments so far: payments + provider network platforms with clear “VPC required” policy.
- Messaging that resonates: “deployment boundaries + audit evidence + predictable latency/cost controls.”
- Messaging that underperforms: generic “faster inference” without regulated context.

What’s blocked / slowing cycle
- Security questionnaires: repeated questions about retention defaults + audit log retention specifics.
- Procurement: SLA + DPA/BAA questions arising earlier than expected in Healthcare.

Decisions / changes to plan
- Update outbound step 2 to include a one-page “Security review starter pack” (links + what to expect) instead of a generic case study placeholder.
- Add a “POC fast path” option: 2–3 week technical evaluation with defined success criteria + weekly check-ins + security touchpoint scheduled in week 1.

Asks (from midpoint)
- Security/GRC: finalize consistent statements for retention + audit logging (so SEs/AEs stop rephrasing).
- Eng/Docs: ensure reference architecture is easily findable from docs security/compliance nav.

Action items (next 7 days)
- Aisha/Olga: ship final language blocks for retention + audit logs (due 2/21)
- Tyler: verify form routing + Slack alerts are firing correctly for both vertical pages (due 2/21)
- Grace: confirm Tier 1 coverage gaps + add contacts (due 2/22)
- Soojin: update decks with “POC fast path” slide + responsibilities matrix (due 2/23)
- Isabelle: prepare midpoint KPI summary for Jordan (due 2/23)

Running list: asset feedback + edits (living)
Landing pages
- Make deployment decision tree explicit: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) and who chooses what when. Owner: Soojin/Ben.
- CTA language: “Request security + architecture review” outperforms “Book a demo” in regulated. Owner: Ben.
- Add “What we’ll cover in the first security call” bullet list. Owner: Ethan/Olga.

Security FAQ addenda
- Replace any absolute statements with configuration-based phrasing (retention, logging). Owner: Olga.
- Add a “NDA required for…” section to set expectations. Owner: Daniel.
- Add short answers for: KMS/HSM integration, SIEM export, SSO/RBAC, audit log access controls. Owner: Marcus.

Pitch decks
- Add “Shared responsibility model” slide early (before deep technical). Owner: Soojin/Simran.
- Add “How we support rollouts + fallback policies in regulated environments” slide. Owner: Markus.

Reference architecture
- Appendix: DNS/TLS and egress allowlist / firewall considerations (include common failure modes). Owner: Simran.
- Add “observability” callouts: token-level metrics, audit pipeline, error analysis, trace hooks. Owner: Markus.

Notes to self (Camila)
- Keep tight weekly loop: what objections did we hear, what asset line changed, and did it change replies.
- If we can’t answer a security question with a link to an approved artifact, we should fix that before scaling.

Next update cadence
- Weekly standup: Tue 11:00 PT (30 min)
- Weekly ABM snapshot in #sales: Thu EOD
- Exec checkpoint: end of week 6–7 (Jordan + stakeholders)
